summary: Service account display-name collision blocks automated secret-rotation and prevents node image pulls in private deploy
description:
Issue summary:
A scheduled secret rotation job failed during the weekly rotation window for two private-deploy customers (prod us-east) after a recent onboarding. Investigation shows the k8s operator's cross-cloud identity normalizer is mapping two distinct cloud service identities to the same internal service-account display name. This produced a name collision in our secret-store key naming and caused the rotation job to overwrite metadata unexpectedly, resulting in stale image-pull credentials on several GKE/eks nodes.

Impact:
- Two private deployments observed 503s and repeated image-pull failures for inference pods between 2026-03-09 01:12 UTC and 2026-03-10 04:50 UTC.
- Customer-facing inference endpoints degraded; autoscaling created new pods that could not start because the node-level image pull failed with permission errors.
- Secret rotation job reported success but new secrets were not applied to node service accounts.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC) in prod us-east (customer tenant IDs masked).
- Kubernetes distributions affected: GKE (private cluster) and EKS nodes in customer-dedicated VPC peering.
- Components involved: k8s-operator v2.3.1, crosscloud-identity-normalizer v1.7.0, secret-rotation-runner v4.0.

Steps to reproduce (summary):
1) Create two distinct cloud identities in different cloud accounts with identical display names (e.g., "redwood-llm-worker-sa").
2) Run the onboarding sync that populates the identity index used by the normalizer.
3) Trigger the secret-rotation-runner for the tenant namespace.
4) Observe that the rotation job writes a single secret key corresponding to the normalized display name and clears previous per-account metadata.

Observed behavior:
- Rotation job logs show success but emitted secret resource points to the wrong cloud identity metadata (account ID mismatched).
- Kubernetes pods fail imagePull with errors referencing unauthorized: "Denied: iam.serviceAccount.get denied" and container runtime logs show pull failure for private registry because image-pull-secret metadata didn't map to the correct KMS-wrapped key.

Expected behavior:
- Normalizer must preserve unique identity namespace (account/project prefix) in secret key generation so different cloud accounts cannot collide on display-name alone.
- Secret rotation should update the correct account-bound image-pull secret and annotate nodes/pods accordingly so kubelet pulls succeed.

Relevant logs / excerpts:
- secret-rotation-runner: "INFO 2026-03-09T01:14:03Z rotation complete: tenant=redacted namespace=ns-abc key=sa-redwood-llm-worker-displayname"
- k8s-operator: "WARN 2026-03-09T01:14:04Z detected display-name collision: normalized_key=sa-redwood-llm-worker-displayname accounts=[acct-111, acct-222]"
- kubelet/containerd: "rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to pull and unpack image \"our-registry/redwood-inference:prod-20260308\": failed to resolve reference: denied: Permission denied (iam.serviceAccounts.get)"

Attachments:
- links to rotation job logs and anonymized kubelet logs were uploaded to the ticket thread and to the private S3 bucket (s3://redwood-support/anonymized/INT-902345/).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Onboard two cloud identities in different provider accounts but set identical display names. 2) Run identity sync. 3) Trigger secret-rotation-runner for tenant namespace. 4) Inspect secret-store keys and node annotations for account mismatch.
logs_excerpt:
k8s-operator WARN: detected display-name collision: normalized_key=sa-redwood-llm-worker-displayname accounts=[acct-111, acct-222]
secret-rotation-runner INFO: rotation complete but metadata.account_id=acct-111 when kubelet expected acct-222
kubelet ERROR: failed to pull image: denied: iam.serviceAccounts.get
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: crosscloud normalizer strips account/project prefix when generating stable keys; recent change in v1.7.0 introduced a regression that prefers display-name deduping across accounts.
What we did so far:
- Replayed onboarding sync in staging with two test accounts and confirmed collision reproduces.
- Confirmed secret-rotation-runner considers only 'normalized_key' when writing secrets and overwrites per-account metadata.
- Verified KMS ciphertexts differ per account; rotation job wrote the ciphertext for acct-111 into the key used by acct-222's pods.
- Temporary mitigation: rolled back crosscloud-identity-normalizer to v1.6.4 for affected clusters; this restored per-account key naming and allowed re-run of rotation which fixed image pull for one tenant.
Open questions:
- Need to confirm if any downstream caches (console token-level breakdowns, on-host secret caches) require invalidation after fix.
- Confirm whether Dedicated provisioning paths also used same normalizer; preliminary scan shows dedicated provisioner uses the same library in onboarding flow.

Next steps planned:
- Patch normalizer to include account/project prefix in generated secret keys (PR in progress).
- Run canary rollout of patched normalizer to one affected prod private-deploy cluster and re-run rotation.
- Create a test asserting collisions are flagged and rotation job fails safe (no overwrite) until manual reconciliation.
- Coordinate with Ops to invalidate node-level secret caches where necessary.
comments: Aisha Patel (reporter) 2026-03-10: Added initial logs and two anonymized kubelet traces. Customer CS alerted us to repeated 503s; internal SLAs triggered immediate escalation.

Marco Rivera (assignee) 2026-03-11: Reproduced locally in staging by creating two GCP service accounts with identical display names. Confirmed rotation writes single key. Rolling back normalizer to v1.6.4 in one cluster restored behavior. Will prepare patch to include account prefix in normalization.

SRE Team (channel #support) 2026-03-11: Applied rollback to two prod private clusters (tenant redacted). Nodes re-registered; some pods still failed until rotation rerun — coordinated with k8s-operator to trigger reapply. Noted that dedicated provisioning may be impacted; we scheduled a scan across dedicated queues.
Security (2026-03-12): Confirmed that no KMS keys were exposed; ciphertexts are distinct. We recommend auditing any automated cleanup that might have removed old secrets during overwrite window.
Marco Rivera 2026-03-13: Opened PR github.com/redwood/k8s-operator/pull/772 to change normalization behavior and added a unit test for collision detection. Will schedule canary for 2026-03-14.
CS (2026-03-13): Customer notified of partial mitigation and ETA for full fix and canary rollout. SLA workaround documented and shared.

Operations (2026-03-13): Flagged follow-up task to scan private-deploy clusters for other potential display-name duplicates and to patch onboarding sync to validate uniqueness constraints before accepting identities.
resolution: Mitigation applied: rolled back normalizer to v1.6.4 in affected clusters to stop overwrites and re-ran secret rotation for impacted tenants. Patch PR available (github.com/redwood/k8s-operator/pull/772) to include account/project prefix in normalized keys and to fail-fast on collisions. Awaiting canary rollout and verification. Post-deploy actions: run full scan of private-deploy tenant identities, add unit/integration tests to onboarding pipeline, and create rollback playbook for future rotation runs.
public_footer: Internal ticket: do not share PII or KMS key materials publicly. For follow-up, see #support and linked confluence runbook.
